title: Assemble a four-piece keyed square panel
instruction: Assemble the four keyed pieces into a flat square at the center of the table.
context: A simplified fixture-free assembly task illustrates choosing orientations and fitting keyed components in a manufacturing workspace.
setup: On a simulated 110 by 130 cm workbench, four loose, rigid, colored components have 50 by 50 by 24 mm square main bodies, each with mass 80 g. Internal mating edges have 12 mm-deep T-shaped tabs, with 14 mm necks, 20 mm heads, distinct offsets and 2 mm nominal clearance; each part has a tab or recess on each of two sides. Four fixed 6 by 6 by 0.5 mm orange corner marks indicate the 100 by 100 mm assembly region centred at world x=0.36 m, y=0. The four bounding-box centres start at (0.190, 0.180), (0.285, 0.205), (0.180, -0.180), and (0.285, -0.205) metres; their yaw angles are 0, 0.40, -0.40 and 0.65 radians, respectively. The table and parts have stylized materials.
scoring: Award 0.25 per piece whose centre is within 4 mm of its specified target in the horizontal plane and height, whose 3-D orientation is within 8 degrees of its target, and whose linear and angular speeds are below 0.01 m/s and 0.5 rad/s respectively. If all four meet their individual targets but any one of the four internal seams differs from its target relative displacement by more than 2 mm along any axis, cap the score at 0.75. Full success requires the 1.0 condition to hold for one second.
reset_notes: Restore the four pieces to the specified fixed initial positions and yaw angles; object jitter is disabled.
fidelity: Stylized rigid parts built from box colliders with approximate friction and 2 mm nominal clearance. The geometry, materials, and physical feasibility have not been validated against fabricated parts. The guided task and manufacturing setting are simplified.
scores: Dream-1: not run. First scripted trial: 0.25/1; a full-score demo has not yet been demonstrated.
